scene: Begin with a complex Fourier coefficient and its conjugate.
Then show how pairs of conjugate-frequency coefficients help produce a real-valued signal.
Once the mathematical relationship is established, introduce your broader question about physical pairs and whether observable relationships reflect deeper symmetry in nature.
The interface could let the visitor compare several kinds of pairing—mathematical conjugacy, reflection, and physical complementarity—and investigate which share formal properties.

source.statement: x̂(ω) = ∫x(t)e^{−iωt}dt. For x = u + iv: x̂(−ω) − conj x̂(ω) = 2i·v̂(−ω). So x̂(−ω) = conj x̂(ω) for every ω ⟺ v = 0 (Fourier uniqueness). Realness is exactly the property that forces the conjugacy
C: x ↦ conj x and C̃: X(ω) ↦ conj X(−ω) are antilinear involutions with F∘C = C̃∘F; real signals = Fix(C), Hermitian-symmetric spectra = Fix(C̃)
conjugate pair ⟺ equal magnitude AND opposite phase (where X ≠ 0); equal magnitude alone ((1+i)e^{−t²/2}) and opposite phase alone (e^{−(ω−1)²/2}e^{iω}) do not give a conjugate pair
X_k = Σx_n e^{−2πikn/N}; for real x: X_{(−k) mod N} = conj X_k; pairs k ↔ N − k
self-paired indices: k = 0 always, k = N/2 iff N even; there X_k is real (phase 0 or π) and the "pair" degenerates to a reality condition on one coefficient; continuous: ω = 0 only
x ↦ (X₀, …, X_⌊N/2⌋) is invertible over ℝ (N real numbers either way); the conjugate half carries no independent information
each pair (X_k, X_{N−k}) is one real oscillation (2/N)|X_k|cos(2πkn/N + arg X_k): one amplitude, one phase; the imaginary parts of the pair cancel identically (a cancellation zero)
for a generic complex-valued signal the symmetry need not hold: x = (1, i, 0, 0) gives X = (1 + i, 2, 1 − i, 0); e^{−t²/2}e^{it} (FB4c)
for a unitary character χ of an abelian group conj χ = χ⁻¹, so a real function has f̂(χ⁻¹) = conj f̂(χ): ℝ (ω ↦ −ω), ℤ_N (k ↦ N − k), ℝ² with η (P ↦ −P) — one structure

forcedBy: x = conj x (realness), and nothing weaker: the defect of the symmetry, x̂(−ω) − conj x̂(ω), is exactly 2i·v̂(−ω), where v = Im x, and v̂ ≡ 0 only for v = 0 (P17Fa).

dispersion.statement: The PDE φ_tt − c²φ_xx + μ²c²φ = 0 (a parameter μ, units 1/length) has plane waves e^{i(kx − ωt)} exactly when ω² = c²k² + μ²c²; its symbol in the project convention is c²k² + μ²c² − ω² = −c²(q(P) − μ²), P = (ω/c, k)
Dimensions: [ω/c] = [k] = [mc/ħ] = L⁻¹, [mc²/ħ] = T⁻¹; ω, k angular (hν = ħω, p = h/λ = ħk)
With μ = mc/ħ: ω² = c²k² + m²c⁴/ħ² ⟺ (ω/c)² − k² = (mc/ħ)²
Convention: the physics positive-frequency wave e^{−iω₀t} sits at −ω₀ in x̂(ω) = ∫x e^{−iωt}dt; "positive frequency" is a convention-dependent label

(ω/c, k) is a pair of coordinates in a plane carrying the Lorentzian quadratic form q = η(P, P); boosts act on it as on (ct, x) because the phase η(P, X) is invariant. It is a relation in frequency-wavevector / energy-momentum variables, not physical spacetime

nulls.relation: q(P) = 0, P ≠ 0 (ω = ±ck, m = 0); ηP ≠ 0, so not a kernel vector
Jv = 0 ⟺ g(θ)v = 0 (a kernel vector of a semidefinite metric)

nullLink: The spectral null P and the spacetime null ray are related only through η: the wave e^{−iη(P, X)} with P null has constant phase along the null ray parallel to P (P17Dd). They are not one kind of zero, and they are not the same object.

massive.statement: m > 0: q(P) = μ² is a hyperbola (1 + 1) with branches ω/c = ±√(k² + μ²); in 1 + 3 a two-sheeted hyperboloid
each branch is one SO⁺(1,1) orbit: the boost with tanh φ = ck/ω (= v_g/c) carries any point to the rest point (μ, 0); boosts never change the branch
the branches are asymptotic to the null cone (ω − c|k| = μ²c²/(ω + c|k|) → 0) and tend to it as μ → 0 at fixed k
frequency gap: no real k for |ω| < μc (evanescent waves); min ω = μc = mc²/ħ at k = 0
proper-time phase rate mc²/ħ along the group worldline, for every k; constant phase along the light ray when m = 0
mass as the orbit invariant: μ = mc/ħ labels the boost orbit as r labels the rotation orbit (#14 chart: Kᵀη + ηK = 0, JᵀI + IJ = 0); μ is not a form parameter like c
massive.status: DERIVED; its reading as a #14 ⇢ #17 connection is PROJECT SYNTHESIS

massAnswer: Does mass appear as a parameter selecting a non-null level set of the same quadratic form whose m=0 case is null? Yes, exactly: m ↦ the level (mc/ħ)² of q = (ω/c)² − k²; m = 0 is the null level (P17Db, P17Dc, P17De). What m changes geometrically: the level and the orbit type (two branches instead of four null half-lines), a frequency gap, the existence of a rest frame, and a Lorentz-invariant proper-time frequency (P17Dg). This does not say that mass is a wave.

posNeg.math: Mathematical Fourier redundancy: the same theorem in two variables. A real field has φ̃(−ω, −k) = conj φ̃(ω, k), i.e. b(k) = conj a(−k) (P17Rb, P17Rc). The partner of (ω, k) is (−ω, −k), not (−ω, k) (P17Rd).
posNeg.condition: It follows from the field being real, and only then: the equation admits complex solutions (P17Re); the reality pairing is available because the operator commutes with conjugation (P17Ra); for iψ_t + αψ_xx = 0 it is not (P17Rf, a PDE contrast only).
posNeg.physical: Physical mode interpretation (classical): a real field's negative-frequency part is fixed by its positive-frequency part; together they make one set of real oscillations. Which half is called positive depends on the sign convention (P17Db, P17Ce).
posNeg.quantum: Quantum particle/antiparticle interpretation: NOT USED. It needs a specific field theory and is recorded as a future branch.
posNeg.answer: For a real classical field the space-time spectrum satisfies φ̃(−ω, −k) = conj φ̃(ω, k): the reality condition pairs the mode at P = (ω/c, k) with the mode at −P, which lies on the same level set of q and on the other branch.

words.realField: For a real classical field the space-time spectrum satisfies φ̃(−ω, −k) = conj φ̃(ω, k): the reality condition pairs the mode at P = (ω/c, k) with the mode at −P, which lies on the same level set of q and on the other branch.
words.massLevel: In the spectral variables P = (ω/c, k) the dispersion relation is the level set q(P) = (mc/ħ)² of the Lorentzian form q = (ω/c)² − k²: m = 0 selects the null level, m > 0 a non-null level whose branches are single boost orbits, with mc/ħ the orbit invariant.

words.restClock: Along the group worldline of any mode on the mass shell the phase advances at mc²/ħ per unit proper time, so the rest frequency mc²/ħ and proper time τ are a Fourier-dual pair; this is duality, not complex conjugacy.
